description: Camera bounds for the Meta_Kim Live control room execution graph. Overview previously refused to shrink below a hardcoded legibility floor of 0.68 on any canvas wider than 1024px, then parked the camera at the top-left inset while the status bar still read Overview. Measured at 1351x726 dpr 1.5 with a content bounding box of 1890x955 in a 1295x382 canvas: fitting needed scale 0.346, the floor forced 0.68, and one of eight node cards was fully visible. The floor is gone. Overview may shrink to the same minScale manual zoom already accepts, and the cell rendering below semanticZoomCellMaxScale carries the small end of the range -- but only since minOnScreenTextPx exists. Removing the floor without it swapped one defect for another: the cell title kept a world-space font size, so at scale 0.28 a 14.42px title measured 4.04px on screen and the reduced rendering was as unreadable as the state it replaced.

policyNotes.fitPaddingPx: Symmetric breathing room between the content bounding box and the canvas edge. The minimap is an overlay pinned bottom-right, so the axis that loses the smaller share of the canvas additionally reserves its measured box; that reserve is computed from the live rect, not declared here.
policyNotes.minScale: One floor shared by overview and manual zoom. Two floors is what produced the defect: manual zoom already accepted 0.28 while overview refused 0.68, so the camera could reach by hand a state it declared illegible by policy.
policyNotes.semanticZoomCellMaxScale: Below this scale the node cards render as a monospace title band instead of full cards. This is what makes a small scale readable, which is why refusing to zoom out was the wrong protection. minScale must stay at or below this value or the cell rendering is unreachable and the shipped CSS for it is dead. The value is not free: it is minOnScreenTextPx divided by the smallest world-space text a full card can declare, which is base.min times the type ladder's smallest step ratio -- 11 / (15 * 0.74) = 0.9910. It sat at 0.42 for the same reason the 0.68 floor sat in code: nobody tied it to the sizes it protects. Measured in a browser at 1760x900, a 17-node run fitted at scale 0.4582, cleared the 0.42 boundary, and drew full cards with all twelve of their text elements between 5.46px and 9.01px against an 11px floor. Normalization now rejects any value below the derived requirement, so the band between the boundary and legibility cannot reopen.
policyNotes.overviewMaxScale: Overview may enlarge a small graph up to this ceiling so a two-node run does not render as two specks, but never past it: a graph blown up past its natural size reads as a zoom bug rather than an overview.
policyNotes.maxScale: Manual zoom ceiling. Overview's ceiling must stay at or below it, otherwise pressing Overview would leave a state the zoom controls cannot return to.
policyNotes.minOnScreenTextPx: The smallest text the camera is allowed to leave on screen, in device-independent pixels after the scale is applied. The type ladder's own floor is a CSS-pixel floor and the camera multiplies CSS pixels by its scale, so the ladder is structurally blind to this failure: at minScale 0.28 the smallest resolvable entity-body step (13.5px against a 16px root) renders 3.78px. The cell title and its band divide this value by the live scale instead of declaring world-space sizes, so the on-screen size is the constant and the world-space size is what moves. It is the same number as the ladder minimumRenderedPixels on purpose: two floors in two coordinate systems is how the 4.04px title passed a suite that already forbade text below 11px. It must stay at or below the ladder's minimumRenderedPixels so the two authorities cannot disagree about the smallest step.
policyNotes.zoomInFactor: One press of the plus control. Paired with zoomOutFactor so a press and its inverse land close to where they started.
policyNotes.zoomOutFactor: One press of the minus control.
policyNotes.wheelZoomInFactor: One wheel notch toward the graph. Smaller than a button press because a wheel emits many notches per gesture, so the same step would overshoot.
policyNotes.wheelZoomOutFactor: One wheel notch away from the graph.
